title: Travel Protection Plans: Claims Timetable by Plan
content:
Four periods govern the timetable of a claim on a Travel Protection Plans certificate. The filing deadline is the calendar days after the incident by which a claim must be filed. The document deadline is the calendar days after filing by which supporting documents must reach the insurer. The decision target is the business days within which the insurer targets a decision. The appeal window is the calendar days after a decision within which the policyholder may appeal.

| Plan | Filing deadline, calendar days from the incident | Document deadline, calendar days from filing | Decision target, business days | Appeal window, calendar days from the decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Trip Basics Essential | 20 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Trip Basics Standard | 20 | 30 | 25 | 30 |
| TripGuard Plus | 30 | 60 | 20 | 45 |
| TripGuard Premier | 45 | 90 | 15 | 60 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | 45 | 90 | 15 | 60 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | 30 | 60 | 20 | 45 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | 60 | 90 | 10 | 90 |

Counting note: the filing deadline, the document deadline and the appeal window are all counted in calendar days, weekends and public holidays included. The decision target alone is counted in business days.

The three calendar periods lengthen as the plan rises, from 20, 30 and 30 days on Trip Basics Essential to 60, 90 and 90 days on Annual Multi-Trip Executive, while the decision target shortens over the same range, from 30 business days to 10.

Hypothetical reading: on TripGuard Plus, a claim arising from an incident must be filed within 30 calendar days of it, and the supporting documents must reach the insurer within 60 calendar days of the filing — the second period running from the filing and not from the incident.
